questions.question: Which broad technological development has helped financial information and transactions move rapidly across national borders?

Information and communication technology, including computer networks and telecommunications
A universal ban on electronic communications
The replacement of all financial records with handwritten ledgers
questions.explanation: Computer networks and telecommunications support rapid cross-border communication and electronic financial services. This is a broad technology application; the chapter’s central examples focus on the role of IT and telecommunications in linking production and services.

questions.subtopic: Special Economic Zones: Land Acquisition Controversy
questions.question: Why has the creation of Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in India sometimes faced severe domestic resistance and protests?
options: Because SEZs refuse to produce manufactured goods
Because foreign MNCs are barred from entering SEZ zones
Because SEZs do not have electricity or road connections
Because fertile multi-crop agricultural land was acquired from farmers, displacing rural families and depriving agricultural labourers of livelihoods
questions.explanation: Setting up SEZs has often involved acquiring fertile farmland, causing loss of agricultural livelihoods and displacement of local communities without adequate rehabilitation.

questions.subtopic: Consumer Culture and Globalisation
questions.question: According to NCERT, what has been one visible effect of globalisation on consumers, particularly well-off urban consumers in India?
options: A complete disappearance of domestic products from every market
A legal requirement to buy only imported goods
A wider choice of goods, with improved quality and lower prices for several products
An end to competition between producers
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that greater competition among local and foreign producers has benefited consumers, particularly well-off urban sections, through greater choice and improved quality and lower prices for several products. The chapter also stresses that the gains have not been shared uniformly.

questions.subtopic: Flexibility of Capital vs Immobility of Labour
questions.question: What fundamental asymmetry exists between capital and labour in the contemporary globalised economy?
options: Human workers can move freely across all borders without passports, while capital is legally locked in home nations
Neither capital nor labour is permitted to cross national borders
Capital and MNC investments can move across borders with tremendous freedom and speed, while human labour faces strict visa restrictions and immigration controls
Multinational corporations are legally prohibited from transferring profits to home countries
questions.explanation: While globalisation has drastically accelerated the movement of goods, capital, and technology across borders, international movement of labour remains severely restricted by national immigration barriers.

questions.subtopic: Role of Judiciary in Protecting Labour Rights
questions.question: When export-oriented factories ignore statutory safety rules and fire workers arbitrarily to lower production costs, what institutional remedy is available in a constitutional democracy?
options: Workers must surrender their citizenship and leave the country
Workers and labour unions can approach labour tribunals and High Courts to enforce statutory rights under the Industrial Disputes Act and Factories Act
Judicial courts are legally prohibited from hearing cases involving foreign MNCs
Workers must seek authorization from the World Trade Organisation
questions.explanation: Democratic judicial institutions (labour courts, High Courts, Supreme Court) possess constitutional authority to strike down arbitrary dismissals and enforce labour welfare protections.

questions.subtopic: Summary: Balanced Globalisation
questions.question: Which statement best reflects NCERT’s assessment of the impact of globalisation in India?
options: Its effects have been uneven: some consumers, skilled workers and firms have benefited, while many small producers and workers have faced difficulties
Every person and every business has benefited equally
Globalisation has had no effect on production, trade or employment
Only foreign companies have benefited, and no Indian producer has gained
questions.explanation: NCERT’s conclusion is that globalisation has benefited well-off consumers and producers with skill, education and wealth, while many small producers and workers have suffered from increased competition. Its impact has not been uniform.
